messages:
maria (support): Hey team — customer ACME Inc on Private (VPC) reporting streaming responses getting truncated after ~25-35s. Client sees partial chunks, then client reconnect loop. They also report intermittent 502/504 from our ALB in front of their origin and a burst of auth failures when reconnects happen. Can someone triage?

maria (support): Repro steps they gave:
```
# simple repro curl (via Cloudflare)
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-open-13b
# client sees some chunks, then long silence, then connection reset, then client retries
```

eli (eng-infra): Thanks — first suspects: ALB idle timeout / target deregistration / proxy buffering (Cloudflare + ALB) causing half-close. Is ALB idle timeout set to default 60s? Also ask them to test bypassing Cloudflare to isolate:
```
# hit origin directly (replace IP)
curl -v -N -H \"Host: api.redwood.example\" http://203.0.113.45:8080/v1/streams?model=gpt-open-13b
```
Also send any nginx/Envoy upstream logs and TCP dumps. Use `curl -N` to avoid libcurl buffering.

zoe (eng-runtime): Additional thought: Cloudflare (and some WAF/edge proxies) will buffer chunked responses until they see a flush or a certain buffer size; if our runtime pauses while awaiting model tokens, edge may hold the connection and then drop it if idle limits differ. We should check:
- ALB idle_timeout vs. Cloudflare edge idle (Cloudflare often enforces its own keepalive/timeout)
- Any gzip/nginx buffering flags (X-Accel-Buffering / proxy_buffering) enabled on origin

Quick check you can ask the customer to run (bypass CF) and then with CF so we can compare timings.

maria (support): Pasted small snippet from their ALB logs and our origin error logs:
```
ALB 2026-11-02T12:34:11.123Z elb-status 504 target:healthcheck=healthy client:10.2.3.4:52345 backend:203.0.113.45:8080 \"GET /v1/streams?model=...\" 0 0 0 0 0 0 - - \"TLSv1.3\" - -
origin nginx: 2026/11/02 12:34:10 [error] 21714#0: *432 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: _, request: \\\"GET /v1/streams?model=...\\\", upstream: \\\"http://127.0.0.1:9000/\\\", host: \\\"api.redwood.example\\\"
```
Also they saw intermittent 401s after repeated reconnects — looks like token rotation + multiple inflight retries caused auth failure counts to rise.

nora (support): For immediate mitigations we pushed to multiple customers:
- Set ALB idle_timeout to 120s (or greater than expected max token generation gap).
- Ensure origin proxy has `proxy_buffering off;` and `proxy_set_header Connection \"keep-alive\";` and `proxy_send_timeout 300s;`
- Add header to disable upstream buffering: `add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;` for nginx.
- Emit lightweight SSE heartbeats every 10-15s from runtime to avoid long silence.
- Client-side: exponential backoff and de-dup token handling to avoid billing duplicate token consumption on reconnects.

nora (support): Example nginx fragment to recommend to customer's ops team:
```
location /v1/streams {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_set_header Connection \"keep-alive\";
  proxy_send_timeout 300s;
  proxy_read_timeout 300s;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  add_header X-Accel-Buffering \"no\";
}
```

eli (eng-infra): Long-term: runtime should emit periodic small comments/heartbeats by default for streaming endpoints (10s) so edges never see long silence. Also add health-aware routing: if ALB shows repeated 5xx for a target, route to a warm fallback to avoid client-visible drop. I'll put together a small test bench to reproduce ALB half-close: use socat to simulate upstream half-close + slow flush and then run curl through ALB.

zoe (eng-runtime): We also noticed cases where gzip compression plus chunking caused edge buffering. Recommend disabling gzip for SSE endpoints or ensure flush after every token chunk. I'll test a patch to force flush on write path.

maria (support): Customer confirms when they bypass Cloudflare and hit origin directly the stream remains stable for longer (no truncation) — so this points to Cloudflare/ALB interaction. They gave pcap + tcpdump which I uploaded to the ticket.

eli (eng-infra): Action items:
- infra: increase ALB idle timeout for ACME target group to 120s (request submitted).
- runtime: add heartbeat toggle and test flush behavior (zoe).
- support: provide temporary credit for duplicate token usage due to reconnect loops (maria/nora).
- ops: ask customer to disable origin buffering on Cloudflare (page rule or worker) while we triage.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary streaming-heartbeat v2.1.9 -> 2 instances (started).

zoe (eng-runtime): I pushed a canary that forces an SSE comment every 8s and explicit fflush after each chunk. Please ask customer to test the canary (we'll route them to the canary host).

maria (support): I'll coordinate with ACME and confirm results. If they still see truncation we'll ask for a short Zoom and collect a live pcap. For now we've: increased ALB timeout, recommended nginx flags, requested Cloudflare buffering off, enabled runtime canary. I'll update the ticket and issue a small billing credit for the reconnect storm. Closing loop once ACME verifies. :thumbsup:
